front.title: MAP Core: Message Envelope, Sessions, Negotiation, and Error Handling

abstract.t: This document defines the mandatory core of the Manolito Agent Protocol (MAP): a signed CBOR/COSE message envelope with deterministic encoding, a version/suite/extension negotiation handshake, session establishment with transport channel binding, replay protection, credit-based flow control, a uniform error taxonomy, the extension framework, and normative bindings to libp2p, QUIC, TCP+TLS, and WebSocket transports. Every other MAP document layers message contents on the envelope defined here.

section.name: Requirements Language
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document family are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here. No adaptation or weakening of these terms applies.

section.name: Overview
section.t: A MAP interaction has two phases. First, peers establish a session: an encrypted, mutually authenticated transport connection (or logical stream) over which they exchange HELLO messages to negotiate a protocol version, cryptographic suite, limits, and extensions. Second, they exchange envelopes — individually signed CBOR messages — whose content field is defined by the companion specifications. Some envelopes (descriptors, receipts, revocations) also travel out of session via DHT storage or gossip; the envelope format is identical, but channel binding is absent and replay rules differ (§7.4).
Design invariants (rationale in 01-design-critique.md C2, C4):

ul.li: I1: Signatures cover the exact transmitted bytes. Verifiers MUST NOT

section.t: re-serialize before verifying.

ul.li: I2: Every envelope is independently verifiable given only the sender's

section.t: key material (self-contained authentication).

ul.li: I3: Unknown non-critical fields are ignored and preserved verbatim when

section.t: a message is stored or forwarded.

ul.li: I4: All normative structures are defined in CDDL [RFC8610] over the

section.t: deterministic CBOR profile of §4.2.

section.name: Cryptographic Suites
section.t: A suite fixes every primitive used by core. Registry: draft-map-ops-01 §3.

Suite 1 is mandatory-to-implement (maximum ecosystem overlap: identical primitives to Noise/TLS1.3/libp2p defaults). Suite 2 is RECOMMENDED where BLAKE3 content addressing dominates. Suite 3 is a placeholder establishing the post-quantum migration path (arch G7); its code point MUST NOT be used until a companion specification defines it. Hash references inside messages use multihash, so mixed-suite meshes interoperate on content addressing.

section.name: Identifiers and Common Types (CDDL)
section.sourcecode: AgentID = bstr .size (34..66) ; multicodec-prefixed public key ; (draft-map-identity-01 §3) MsgID = bstr .size 16 ; cryptographically random per message SessionID = bstr .size 16 TaskID = bstr .size 32 ; requester-chosen; see tasks §3 Multihash = bstr ; per multiformats/multihash CapURI = tstr .regexp "map:cap:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9/._-]{0,126}" Timestamp = uint ; milliseconds since Unix epoch, UTC Version = uint ; (major << 8) | minor; 0x0100 = 1.0 ZoneLabel = uint .le 3 ; arch §8.1 ExtMap = { * int => any } ; extension key registry: ops §3

section.name: Structure
section.t: Every MAP message is a COSE_Sign1 [RFC9052] object, CBOR tag 18:

The signature is computed per COSE over Sig_structure = ["Signature1", protected, external_aad, payload] encoded with §4.2. external_aad is the channel-binding token (§7.3) for in-session messages and the empty byte string for out-of-session objects.

section.name: Deterministic encoding profile
section.t: All CBOR that is signed, hashed, or content-addressed MUST use RFC 8949 §4.2.1 core deterministic encoding: shortest-form integers, definite-length strings/arrays/maps only, map keys sorted bytewise on their encoded form, no duplicate keys. Floating-point values MUST NOT appear in signed structures; quantities that are conceptually fractional use integer milli-/micro-units or CBOR decimal fractions (tag 4) with integer mantissa and exponent. Per invariant I1, this profile governs producers; verifiers operate on received bytes and additionally MUST reject envelopes violating the profile (malleability defense).

section.name: Validation rules (every receiver, every envelope)

ol.li: Well-formed CBOR; tag 18; 4-element array; sizes within negotiated

section.t: limits (§6.3) — else error 1000/1004.

ol.li: Body[0] equals the negotiated version (in-session) or a supported

section.t: version (out-of-session) — else 1001.

ol.li: All keys listed in crit are understood — else 1002.
Timestamp within ±120 s of local clock (in-session) or within object

section.t: class freshness rules (out-of-session) — else 1003.

ol.li: Signature verifies against kid, or against the leaf key of a valid

section.t: delegation chain terminating at kid's root (identity §6) — else 2000/2003.

ol.li: Sender authorization for msg-type in current state (per companion spec)

section.t: — else 2005. Failing envelopes MUST NOT cause state transitions; receivers SHOULD respond with ERROR (in-session) and MUST rate-limit error responses.

section.name: Message Types (initial registry)

tr.td: Core: HELLO 0x0001, HELLO_ACK 0x0002, PING 0x0003, PONG 0x0004, CLOSE 0x0005, ERROR 0x0006, FLOW_CREDIT 0x0007
Discovery: DESCRIPTOR 0x0100, STATUS_QUERY 0x0101, STATUS_REPORT 0x0102, CAP_QUERY 0x0103, CAP_RESPONSE 0x0104

Tasks: OFFER 0x0200, QUOTE 0x0201, ASSIGN 0x0202, ACCEPT 0x0203, REJECT 0x0204, CHUNK 0x0205, TOOL_CALL 0x0207, TOOL_GRANT 0x0208, TOOL_RESULT 0x0209, CHECKPOINT 0x020A, CHECKPOINT_ACK 0x020B, CANCEL 0x020C, COMPLETE 0x020D, RESUME 0x020E, RESERVE 0x020F, LEASE 0x0210, LEASE_RELEASE 0x0211
Trust: RECEIPT 0x0300, RECEIPT_ACK 0x0301, EVIDENCE_QUERY 0x0302, EVIDENCE_SET 0x0303, CHALLENGE 0x0304, CHALLENGE_RESPONSE 0x0305
Pay: PAY_QUOTE 0x0400, PAY_AGREE 0x0401, PAY_INVOICE 0x0402, PAY_PROOF 0x0403, PAY_RECEIPT 0x0404, PAY_DISPUTE 0x0405, PAY_DISPUTE_EVIDENCE 0x0406

section.t: 0x0206 is deliberately unassigned (a hole between CHUNK 0x0205 and TOOL_CALL 0x0207; never to be reused — ops §3.3).
Registration policy for new code points: Specification Required (draft-map-ops-01 §3).

section.name: Extension Keys (initial registry)
section.t: Extensions are negotiated in HELLO (§6.1 key 3) before use and keyed by these code points; each is fully specified in its owning document. Points are immutable once assigned (ops §3.3); ≥ 0xF000 is private-use.

section.name: HELLO / HELLO_ACK
section.t: The connection initiator sends HELLO as its first envelope:
section.sourcecode: Hello = { 1 => [+ Version], ; supported protocol versions, descending pref 2 => [+ uint], ; supported suites, descending pref 3 => { * int => uint }, ; offered extensions: ext-key => max ext-version 4 => uint, ; max-message-size accepted (bytes; >= 65536) ? 5 => uint, ; max concurrent tasks accepted ? 6 => bstr .size 32, ; cookie (retry/DoS defense, §6.5) ? 7 => [* ZoneLabel] ; zones the sender is willing to operate in }
section.t: The responder selects the highest mutually supported version, the first mutually supported suite in the initiator's preference order, and the intersection of extensions, replying HELLO_ACK:
section.sourcecode: HelloAck = { 1 => Version, ; chosen 2 => uint, ; chosen suite 3 => { * int => uint }, ; accepted extensions with chosen versions 4 => uint, ; responder's max-message-size ? 5 => uint, ? 8 => bstr ; transcript-hash: H(HELLO bytes || this map } ; fields 1..5 deterministically encoded)
section.t: Note the field-shape asymmetry under identical field numbers: Hello fields 1/2 are lists (offered sets) while HelloAck fields 1/2 are singletons (the chosen values) — implementers regularly miss this; TV-001/TV-003 are the byte-level guard.

If no version or suite is mutual, the responder sends ERROR 1001 with the supported sets and closes. Both peers MUST verify each envelope's signer matches the transport-authenticated identity (§7.3) — the HELLO exchange is therefore itself authenticated and MITM-resistant.

The initiator's HELLO envelope carries a fresh SessionID (Body key 6); the responder MUST echo the same SessionID in its HELLO_ACK envelope, and every subsequent in-session envelope carries it. A SessionID mismatch is a state violation (1006) and the session MUST be closed.

section.name: Downgrade resistance
section.t: Both peers compute the negotiation transcript hash TH = H("MAPv1-transcript" || HELLO-envelope-bytes || HELLO_ACK-envelope-bytes) with the chosen suite's hash. TH is mixed into the channel-binding token (§7.3). An attacker who strips versions/suites from either HELLO alters TH and every subsequent signature check fails — closing threat TH14.

section.name: Limits
section.t: Default/floor limits: max-message-size 256 KiB (floor 64 KiB); larger payloads MUST use chunked CHUNK streams or content-addressed fetch. Peers MUST enforce their advertised limits and MUST NOT send beyond the peer's. Receivers SHOULD enforce the size limit on the raw received frame before any decoding or signature work (cheapest check first; DoS posture §6.5).

section.name: Version policy
section.t: Version is (major, minor). Minor revisions are strictly additive (new optional fields, new msg-types); implementations MUST accept unknown optional Body keys and unknown msg-types within a session by replying ERROR 3000 without closing. Major revisions may break anything and never interoperate implicitly. Deprecation process: draft-map-ops-01 §3.4.

section.name: Denial-of-service posture at handshake
section.t: Responders under load MAY reply to HELLO with ERROR 1005 carrying a cookie; the initiator retries HELLO including the cookie, proving reachability before the responder allocates session state (cf. DTLS/QUIC retry). Signature verification precedes all allocation-heavy processing.

section.name: Message-level
section.t: Receivers maintain, per sender, a cache of MsgIDs seen within the last 10 minutes and MUST reject duplicates (1003) and out-of-window timestamps. The cache bound is enforceable because of rate limits (§8.3).

section.name: Session sequence numbers
section.t: In-session envelopes carry seq, starting at 0 per direction and incrementing by 1. Receivers MUST reject non-monotonic seq (1003). seq gives cheap ordering across multiplexed transports and makes transcript audits (tasks §8) unambiguous.

section.name: Channel binding
section.t: On session establishment each peer derives CB = HKDF(TH, transport-exporter, "map cb", 32) where transport-exporter is: the TLS 1.3 exporter (EXPORTER-map-binding) for TLS/QUIC transports; the Noise handshake hash for Noise transports; for transports lacking an exporter, the concatenation of both peers' static public keys as authenticated by the transport. CB is the COSE external_aad for every in-session envelope. Consequences: an envelope recorded on one session cannot verify on another (anti-relay), and the signer is cryptographically bound to the transport-authenticated endpoint (TH4). The transport identity MUST equal the envelope kid's key or a delegated key chained to it (identity §6); mismatch is error 2000 and immediate CLOSE.

section.name: Out-of-session objects
section.t: Descriptors, revocations, receipts, and other store-and-forward objects use empty external_aad, MUST carry ttl-ms, and are deduplicated by content address; freshness/supersession rules are per object class (e.g., descriptor seq, discovery §5.3).

section.name: Credit-based streaming
section.t: Any message family that streams (task CHUNKs, evidence sets) is governed by receiver-granted credit. FLOW_CREDIT content:

Senders MUST NOT exceed outstanding credit in either unit; violations are 1005 and MAY be receipt-recorded. Initial credits are granted in ASSIGN/ACCEPT (tasks §4). Rationale: transport backpressure alone lets a slow or malicious reader pin provider resources (VRAM, queue slots) indefinitely — critique "no flow control". Credit lets providers bound commitment and bill for reserved-but-unconsumed output.

section.name: Keepalive
section.t: PING/PONG carry an opaque 8-byte payload echoed verbatim; RECOMMENDED interval 30 s on idle sessions; 3 missed PONGs ⇒ session failure handling.

section.name: Rate limits
section.t: Implementations MUST enforce configurable per-peer ceilings on: envelopes/s, HELLOs/min from an address, STATUS_QUERYs/min, and DHT-record ingestion/s, with 1005 + exponential backoff hints (retry-after-ms in ERROR detail).

section.name: Error Handling
section.t: ERROR content:
section.sourcecode: ErrorMsg = { 1 => uint, ; code 2 => bool, ; retryable ? 3 => tstr, ; human-readable (English; not for machines) ? 4 => MsgID, ; message being answered ? 5 => { * int => any } ; machine-readable detail (per-code schema) }
section.t: Code space (registry; Specification Required):
1002 unknown critical extension, 1003 replay/out-of-window/bad-seq, 1004 message too large, 1005 rate limited / no credit, 1006 state violation.

object, 2002 revoked key, 2003 invalid delegation chain, 2004 zone violation, 2005 not authorized for message type, 2006 countersignature refused (the receiver declines to attest the sender's claimed facts — e.g. receipt usage/timestamps outside countersignature tolerance, trust §3).
unavailable, 3002 context too large, 3003 ontology term unknown.
memory/VRAM class, 4003 reservation expired, 4004 storage exhausted.
5002 cancelled, 5003 checkpoint invalid, 5004 tool denied, 5005 output policy violation, 5006 resumption impossible.

settlement failed, 6003 dispute opened, 6004 method unsupported, 6005 authorized cap exceeded (PayAgree.4), 6006 agreement digest mismatch (quote/agreement envelope digest does not match the referenced bytes — price-switch defense, pay §3.1), 6007 task binding mismatch (a pay message's task binding ≠ the bound task: PayQuote.9 vs the OFFER's TaskID, pay §3; UsageWatermark.1 vs the agreement's task, pay §4.1), 6008 invalid payment proof (forged or mismatched settlement proof, pay §5), 6009 invoice-watermark violation (a metered invoice's UsageWatermark fails a pay §4.1 check: presence, monotonicity, meter consistency, or billing arithmetic), 6010 escrow violation (a terms-1/2 invoice or receipt fails a pay §5.2 check: phase presence, prepaid/hold amount ≠ quoted total, premature or oversized release, duplicate hold, or an unrecognized receipt kind). 6002 remains the generic settlement failure for causes not covered by a specific code.

Retryability semantics: retryable = true means the identical request MAY succeed later at the same peer; false means the requester MUST change something (peer, parameters, payment) — this drives orchestrator fallback logic deterministically (adopting design3's TTFT/fallback discipline).

section.name: Transport Bindings
section.t: Common requirements: mutual authentication with keys verifiable against AgentIDs; confidentiality and integrity; ordered byte streams; multiplexing (or one connection per session). Envelope framing on raw streams: 4-byte big-endian length prefix, then envelope bytes; length MUST respect negotiated max-message-size.

ul.li: libp2p (RECOMMENDED): protocol ID /map/1.0.0; security Noise or

section.t: TLS; muxer yamux; transports QUIC-v1 preferred, TCP, WebSocket, WebTransport. PeerID MUST equal the AgentID key (identity §3.2). NAT traversal profile — AutoNAT v2, Circuit Relay v2, DCUtR hole punching — is REQUIRED for public-mesh providers (discovery §10). One MAP session runs per /map/1.0.0 substream, length-prefixed as above.

Channel binding for /map/1.0.0 (§7.3 third clause — transports lacking an exporter): rust-libp2p does not portably expose a Noise handshake-hash / TLS-exporter equivalent on its stream API, so the exporter for this binding is initiator-AgentID || responder-AgentID (the two PeerIDs the connection authenticated, in stream-initiator-first order). This binds the session to the authenticated identities of both endpoints. Residual (acknowledged, weaker than a true exporter): it binds the identity pair, not the specific connection instance, so it does not by itself separate two concurrent connections between the same pair; the per-message msg-id replay cache and the monotonic in-session sequence numbers (§7.1) prevent cross-connection replay within the window regardless. An implementation whose libp2p version exposes Noise handshake-hash material SHOULD use it instead and record that choice.

ul.li: Raw QUIC: ALPN map/1; TLS 1.3 with RawPublicKey or self-signed

section.t: X.509 carrying the Ed25519 key; exporter per §7.3.

ul.li: TCP+TLS 1.3: ALPN map/1; same certificate rules.
WebSocket: subprotocol map.v1; binary frames = framed envelopes;

section.t: over TLS; where the WS layer terminates TLS at an intermediary, CB falls back to static-key binding and the session MUST be treated as Zone ≥2.

ul.li: gRPC binding (OPTIONAL, non-normative appendix in tasks): bulk CHUNK

section.t: streaming MAY be carried over gRPC for ecosystem convenience; every gRPC message remains a MAP envelope (I2 holds regardless of carrier).

section.name: Extension Framework
section.t: Extension keys are integers from the MAP Extension Registry (ops §3). Rules: (a) unknown keys absent from crit MUST be ignored and, for stored/ forwarded objects, preserved byte-exactly (I3); (b) keys present in crit MUST be understood or the envelope rejected with 1002; (c) extensions are version-negotiated in HELLO field 3 before use in-session; (d) extensions MUST NOT redefine core field semantics. This mirrors the proven HTTP/TLS/COSE evolution model and is the mechanism by which bidding, KV-cache transfer, Git workspace sync, etc. attach without core changes.

section.name: Session State Machine
section.t: ESTABLISHED admits all in-session message families per negotiated conformance classes. CLOSE content carries an ErrorMsg-shaped reason. Half-close is not modeled; either CLOSE tears down the session after flushing acknowledged state (task-level survival across sessions is handled by tasks §8 resumption, not by the session layer).

section.name: Examples and Test Vectors
section.t: TV-001 (signed HELLO envelope, 166 bytes) and TV-002 (dual-signed ExecutionReceipt) in test-vectors/map-test-vectors.md are normative encoding examples generated with real Ed25519 keys; all signatures verify per §4. Implementations MUST reproduce byte-identical Sig_structures from the listed inputs.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Covered throughout: bytes-not-objects verification (§4, I1), deterministic encoding as malleability defense (§4.2), downgrade resistance (§6.2), handshake DoS (§6.5), replay and relay (§7), resource pinning (§8), information leakage via error verbosity (ERROR detail MUST NOT echo payload contents to unauthenticated peers). Residual: timestamp windows assume ±120 s clock sanity; deployments with worse clocks MUST widen windows and accept the enlarged replay cache, or deploy roughtime.

Channel-binding strength depends on the transport (§7.3, §10). The anti-relay and endpoint-binding guarantees of §7.3 are only as strong as the transport-exporter fed into the CB derivation. On transports that expose a true key-schedule exporter (TLS 1.3, raw QUIC — §10) CB binds the specific connection instance. On transports lacking a portable exporter — notably the /map/1.0.0 libp2p binding as currently implemented, whose exporter is the authenticated initiator-AgentID || responder-AgentID pair (§10) — CB binds the identity pair but not the specific connection, so it does not by itself separate two concurrent connections between the same pair; §7.1's per-message msg-id replay cache and monotonic in-session sequence numbers carry that separation within the window. Deployments requiring instance-level binding MUST use an exporter-bearing transport (TLS/QUIC) or a libp2p stack that surfaces Noise handshake-hash material, and SHOULD treat the identity-pair fallback as Zone ≥2. This is an implementation-maturity limitation of the reference libp2p binding, not a wire-format constraint: the CB derivation (§7.3) is unchanged across transports, so a stronger exporter drops in without a protocol change.

section.name: IANA-Style Considerations
section.t: This document establishes (initial contents above; policies in ops §3): MAP Cryptographic Suites; MAP Message Types; MAP Body Keys; MAP Extension Keys; MAP Error Codes; MAP Transport Bindings (ALPN/protocol-ID strings). The assigned values and the full family-wide index are in draft-map-wire-01.md §3.1, §3.2, §3.3, §3.4, §3.5, and §3.6 respectively; in case of divergence the normative tables above govern.
